description: Small baseline benchmark for evaluating semantic retrieval in the Research & Knowledge Assistant.

chunks.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines information retrieval with language generation. It retrieves relevant external documents and provides their content as context to a language model, helping produce grounded answers.
A typical RAG pipeline consists of document ingestion, text chunking, embedding generation, vector storage, similarity-based retrieval, and answer generation using retrieved context.
A vector database stores numerical vector representations of data. It supports similarity search by comparing query embeddings with stored embeddings to identify semantically similar content.

Metadata filtering restricts vector search results using attributes such as document identifiers, filenames, or page numbers. Combining metadata filters with semantic similarity search helps narrow retrieval to a relevant subset.
Text embedding models convert text into dense numerical vectors. Semantically similar sentences should have vector representations that are close to each other in the embedding space.
Dense retrieval encodes queries and documents into vectors using an embedding model. The retriever compares these vectors using a similarity measure to find relevant document passages.
